araññajā.meaning_2: born in the forest; forest-born; growing in the wilderness
araññajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes trees (rukkhā) in the verses. Nominative plural agreeing with rukkhā.
araññajā.translation_1: the trees born in the forest.
araññajā.example_2: 74. Sādhū sambahulā ñātī, api rukkhā araññajā;
araññajā.translation_2: 74. “United, forest-like, should kinsfolk stand; even trees born in the forest are good [when together];

umhayate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present in the text; the prefix u- is rare and the form is irregular. The object is in the accusative (naṃ).

cīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ci (nominative singular of the pronominal/interrogative stem kiṃ, 'who?') and idha ('here'); used as a relative in the verses: yo cīdha = 'whoever here'. Sometimes analysed as cī + idha, but ci is the standard form.
cīdha.translation_2: Who here accepts the truth after examination,

āmanta.meaning_2: farewell; addressing; taking leave (of); "I bid you farewell"
āmanta.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the fixed phrase āmanta kho taṃ gacchāma/gacchāmi, a parting formula. Probably a shortening of āmantayitvā or an absolutive of āmanteti ('having addressed, having taken leave'), used idiomatically as an indeclinable; the PEU entry analyses it as ā + manta + tvā. Kept as indeclinable, not as a verb form.

bhumyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular; bhumyā is the sandhi form with the locative ending -yā. In the text it means 'on the ground'.

nivātajā.meaning_2: growing in a sheltered place; grown in a windless spot; sheltered (of plants)
nivātajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse nivātajā agrees with rukkhā in mama passe nivātajā, 'the trees growing in my sheltered place'. Sometimes analysed as nivāta + jana + kvi, but here ja (from √jan 'be born, grow') fits the metre and meaning.
nivātajā.example_2: 124. Te rukkhā saṃvirūhanti, mama passe nivātajā;
nivātajā.translation_2: Those trees will sprout from seeds protected from the wind upon my branches;

kavacamabhihessati.meaning_2: will strike; will attack; will smite (against)
kavacamabhihessati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is resolved by sandhi from kavacaṃ abhihessati. The future stem hessa- comes from abhihanati (abhi + √han) with the s-future element, contracted.
kavacamabhihessati.example_2: Yattha rājā rājakumāro vā, kavacamabhihessati achambhito [asambhīto (sī. syā. pī.)].
kavacamabhihessati.translation_2: Where a king or a prince, fearless, will strike against the armor of an enemy.

nūnasā.meaning_2: surely she; indeed she; she must be
nūnasā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the emphatic particle nūna and the pronoun sā. In the verse sā nūnasā kapaṇikā = "she surely is a miserable one". A variant of nūna is nūnā.
nūnasā.translation_2: 4. She must be a miserable one, blind and without a guide;

dāmāto.meaning_2: from a rope; from a bond; from a tether
dāmāto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular of dāma (rope, bond, tether). In the text, muttā dāmāto means "freed from the rope". Alternative reading mutto ca bandhanā.
dāmāto.example_1: 8. Mutto ca bandhanā nāgo, muttamādāya kuñjaro [kāsirājena pesito (sī. syā.), mutto dāmāto kuñjaro (pī. sī. niyya)];
dāmāto.translation_1: 8. Freed from bonds, the bull elephant, the elephant set free,

māhitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the Jātaka verse; the accepted text has āhatvā, from āharati (√har). The commentary glosses it as drawing water with the trunk.
māhitvā.translation_1: Having drawn water with his trunk, he sprinkled his mother.

koya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ko + ayaṃ (nominative singular of pronoun ka). Often written koyaṃ; here the final consonant is elided before the following vowel in verse. First word of the verse line.
koya.example_1: 10. Koya anariyo devo, akālenapi vassati [akālena pavassati (sī. syā.), akālena ’ tivassati (pī.)];
koya.translation_1: 10. Who is this ignoble sky-deity that rains even out of season?

tyāhamatrajo.meaning_2: I am the son of a rival wife; I, the son of my co-wife, have come
tyāhamatrajo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tya (pora; 'of another') + ahaṃ ('I') + atraja ('son of oneself', i.e. legitimate son; atraja = atta + ja). The whole group is glossed as 'I am the son of a rival wife'. Alternative split: tya + ahaṃ + atrajo.
tyāhamatrajo.example_2: 11. Uṭṭhehi amma kiṃ sesi, āgato tyāhamatrajo;
tyāhamatrajo.translation_2: 11. Rise, mother! Why do you lie there? I, your legitimate son, have arrived;

gantabya.meaning_2: to be gone; that should be gone; to be gone past; to be passed by
gantabya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written gantabya in this edition (ka. variant gantabba). Here the ptp is used impersonally in the phrase 'gantabbaṃ āhu' — 'they said one should not go (past)'.
gantabya.example_1: Na brāhmaṇe addhike tiṭṭhamāne, gantabba [gantabya (ka.)] māhu dvipadinda [dipadāna (sī. pī.), dvipadāna (syā.)] seṭṭha.
gantabya.translation_1: “Wise ones have said that one should not pass by a brahmin standing as a wayfarer, O Lord of bipeds.”

āpūratī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has āpūratī with the emphatic -ti (āpūrati iti). 3rd singular present.
āpūratī.example_2: Āpūratī kāsipatī tathāhaṃ, tayāpi me saṅgamo ajja laddhoti.
āpūratī.translation_2: “I am filled, O Lord of Kasi, in that way; today I have gained an association with you.”

atibalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of ati (very) + bala (strength). In the text it describes saccanikkama, 'of true resolution'; nominative singular.
atibalo.example_2: Pāyāsi vitto [citto (syā.)] abhiruyha sandanaṃ, maggeneva atibalo saccanikkamo.
atibalo.translation_2: Joyful, the very strong one of true resolution mounted his chariot and marched out along the way.

jahātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative spelling jahātī in the text; jahati is also found. Third person singular present of hāti (to abandon).
jahātī.example_1: Tañcāpi jahati [jahāti (sī. syā. pī.), jahātī (?)] avītarāgo, udaye mā pamāda carassu dhammaṃ.
jahātī.translation_1: Even that, one not free from lust abandons, O Udaya, do not be careless, walk in piety.

vijigucchiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular in the text (vijigucchiṃ), not present 3rd singular. The form shows the vowel i added between vi and the root. Some patterns give the 3rd singular present as vijigucchati.
vijigucchiṃ.example_2: Tena pacchā vijigucchiṃ, taṃ pāpaṃ pakataṃ mayā;
vijigucchiṃ.translation_2: Later, I felt disgust for that evil I had done;

tampalohaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears as tampalohaṃ in the text (nominative or accusative singular); the variant reading and comment explain it as 'taṃ palohaṃ' i.e. that molten (metal). Sometimes analysed as a compound with 'loha' (copper/metal).
tampalohaṃ.translation_1: Like molten copper, sensual pleasures are more painful than those.

nipāletuṃ.meaning_2: to prevent; to ward off; to protect against
nipāletuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive (pos inf, gramm 'inf of nipāleti') meaning 'to prevent, to ward off' in the verse; the PEU gloss 'to take care' reflects the root pāl but the context is 'cannot prevent'. Cf. nipāletuṃ = ni + pāl + *e + tuṃ.
nipāletuṃ.example_2: 86. Yaṃ na sakkā nipāletuṃ, posena lapataṃ bahuṃ;
nipāletuṃ.translation_2: “That which a mortal cannot prevent, though he may lament much,

mattanā.meaning_2: measured; limited; of measure; to the extent (of); merely
mattanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular of matta, here in the phrase hiṃsamattānamattano (harming himself to the extent of). The variant mattanā is the instrumental of mattā / matta. Not from √mad; the meaning is measured, limited, to the extent of.
mattanā.example_1: 91. Kiso vivaṇṇo bhavati, hiṃsamattānamattano [mattanā (sī. aṭṭha. su. ni.590)];
mattanā.translation_1: He becomes emaciated and pale, tormenting himself;

juṇhaka.meaning_2: Juṇhaka (name of a lunar day or fortnight); (or) name of a Brahmin; name of a Nāga
juṇhaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A name in a list of names in the Yuddhakathā Jātaka verse. Possibilities: name of a lunar day (juṇha = full-moon day; see juṇhaka); name of a Brahmin; or name of a Nāga. The PEU entry is uncertain. In the text it is part of a compound or list; the word is not inflected.
juṇhaka.translation_2: Siri, Mātuposaka, Nāgavara, again Juṇhaka, Dhammamudayavara,

kannappakannaṃ.meaning_2: shifting here and there; ever-changing; (lit.) ear and reverse-ear
kannappakannaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the simile kannappakannaṃ yathā rukkhachāyā, describing something unstable like tree shade. The PEU suggests kannappakanṇa 'constantly inhaling and exhaling'; the text's single -n- may be a variant. Used adverbially in the verse.
kannappakannaṃ.example_2: 4. Thīnañhi cittaṃ yathā vānarassa, kannappakannaṃ yathā rukkhachāyā;
kannappakannaṃ.translation_2: For the mind of women is like that of a monkey, like the shade of a tree that shifts hither and thither;

menaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] menaṃ is most likely me + naṃ (enaṃ), the emphatic/demonstrative particle naṃ attached to the pronoun me; some analyse it as na + imaṃ. In the verses it refers to the horse that is being led on with soft words. The PEU entries medhā and megha are unrelated.

dubbidu.meaning_2: difficult to know; hard to understand
dubbidu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse tesaṃ have dubbidu sabbabhāvo, dubbidu agrees with sabbabhāvo. The reading dubbidu may be a metrical or dialectal variant of dubbidū (du + vidū), and the commentary's variant saccabhāvo suggests some uncertainty. Confirmed as an adjective; not the homonym dubbidha ("of two kinds").
dubbidu.example_2: Ete naro niccayato [niccayatto (sī. pī.)] bhajetha, tesaṃ have dubbidu sabbabhāvo [saccabhāvo (syā.)].
dubbidu.translation_2: A person should follow these with caution, for their true nature is indeed hard to know.

etitthiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of etā (nominative plural feminine of eta) and itthiyo (nominative plural of itthī). In the text the following pañca agrees with itthiyo. Sometimes written as etā itthiyo.

tyāssūni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tya (poetic for te, "your") + assūni (neuter plural of assu, "tears"). Nominative plural in the verse; some analyses read tyassūni with a single s.
tyāssūni.example_2: Kena tyāssūni vattanti, kuto taṃ bhayamāgataṃ.
tyāssūni.translation_2: Whence come thy fears, why flow the tears in which thine eyes are bathed?”

vichindatha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd plural imperative with vi- prefix; variant reading vichindatha in the Pī. edition, emphasizing severing completely.
vichindatha.example_1: 19. Agge ca chetvā majjhe ca, pacchā mūlamhi chindatha [mūlañca chindatha (sī.), mūlaṃ vichindatha (pī.)];
vichindatha.translation_1: “Cut first the crown, the middle next, then last the root of me;

tepihaṃ.meaning_2: there; in that respect; by that
tepihaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Verse word, possibly a sandhi or emphatic formation (te + pi + haṃ?); meaning uncertain, glossed from context. Maybe read as tesaṃ pi haṃ.
tepihaṃ.translation_2: These I should crush by one huge fall,—and great would be their woe.”

tipañcarattūpagatamhi.meaning_2: when the moon has reached the fifteenth night; when the full moon has arrived
tipañcarattūpagatamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tipañcarattūpagata (adj, comp) and amhi (locative of ahaṃ? actually locative of adj). Locative singular in the text. See tipañcarattūpagata.
tipañcarattūpagatamhi.translation_1: “When the fifteenth day full moon has risen,
tipañcarattūpagatamhi.example_2: 26. Tipañcarattūpagatamhi cande, vego mahā hehiti sāgarassa;
tipañcarattūpagatamhi.translation_2: When the moon has reached the third night, there will be a great surge of the ocean;

āputtaputtehi.meaning_2: with children and grandchildren; together with sons of sons; down to the sons of grandsons
āputtaputtehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare compound, glossed as ā + putta + putta ("unto sons of sons"); instrumental plural āputtaputtehi in the verse. ā- here has the sense "down to, including".
āputtaputtehi.translation_1: Celebrate, even unto the sons of sons!”
āputtaputtehi.example_2: Na vo bhayaṃ paṭipassāmi kiñci, āputtaputtehi pamodathavho.
āputtaputtehi.translation_2: I see no fear for you at all; rejoice together with your children and sons.

paviceyya.meaning_2: should examine; should investigate; should contemplate
paviceyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular optative in -eyya, used in the verse in the sense of examining and taking (tacchaṃ gaṇhati). The PEU analysis as an absolutive in -tvā does not fit the syntax; the optative fits.
paviceyya.translation_1: Who here accepts the truth after examination,
paviceyya.example_2: Yo cīdha tacchaṃ [majjhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.)] paviceyya gaṇhati [gaṇhi (ka.)], sa ve naro seṭṭhamupeti ṭhānaṃ.
paviceyya.translation_2: The person who examines and takes what is accurate reaches the highest state.

byadhesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist or present 2nd singular in the verse (mā ... byadhesi); PEU analyses as byadha + ṇi + si, causative of bādhati with vi-.
byadhesi.translation_1: ‘Let what must be done not harm me on the day the duty ripens.’
byadhesi.example_2: 36. Anāgataṃ paṭikayirātha kiccaṃ,‘‘ mā maṃ kiccaṃ kiccakāle byadhesi ’’;
byadhesi.translation_2: One should do the work of the future beforehand, 'lest the work distress me at the time of work';

byadhetīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs as byadhetīti = byadheti + iti at the end of the verse; the sandhi -ī- is due to the following iti. The form shows the Eastern /y/ for /j/ (byādheti for bādheti), causative of √bādh.
byadhetīti.translation_1: is not harmed by what must be done on the day the duty ripens.”
byadhetīti.example_2: Taṃ tādisaṃ paṭikata [paṭikataṃ (ka.), paṭigata (sī. aṭṭha.), paṭikacca (?)] kiccakāriṃ, na taṃ kiccaṃ kiccakāle byadhetīti.
byadhetīti.translation_2: That work does not distress that person who is a doer of work done beforehand at the time of work.

usīnnara.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name, a variant reading of usīnara (as also usīnaka). Vocative singular in the text, addressing the king.
usīnnara.example_1: 62. Nāyaṃ migānamatthāya, usīnaka [usīnara (sī. pī.), usīnnara (syā.)] bhavissati;
usīnnara.translation_1: This is not for hunting game, Usīnara;

tantrañca.meaning_2: and the sacrificial rite; and the sacrificial text
tantrañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text variant for yaññatantañca, i.e. yañña + tanta + ca. yaññatanta ('sacrificial rite') + -ca, with the sandhi -aṃ + c- > -añc-. Locative absolute phrase with adhicca vede.
tantrañca.example_1: 66. Adhicca vede [vedaṃ (ka.)] sāvittiṃ, yaññatantañca [tantrañca (sī. syā. pī.)] brāhmaṇā;
tantrañca.translation_1: When brahmins, having studied the Vedas, the Sāvittī, and the sacrificial rites,

nosi.meaning_2: you are not; you are not
nosi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of no (not) + asi (you are). Written nosi; alternative analysis no + si. Occurs three times in the verses.
nosi.example_2: tvaṃ nosi rājā bhava me sukhāya”.

upāramāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular present in the text (upāramāmi), so the ending is -mi, not -ti. The meaning is 'I refrain / abstain'.
upāramāmi.example_2: 92. Esāhamajjeva upāramāmi, na cāpihaṃ [na cāpahaṃ (sī. pī.)] kiñci kareyya pāpaṃ;
upāramāmi.translation_2: I will refrain this very day, and I would not do any evil;

paṭisandhāya.meaning_2: having connected; having joined together; having formed a bond; having become attached
paṭisandhāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -ya in the verse; the PET entry's 'trust and thorough' is a guess. The sense with caranti is 'go about joined together, mutually connected'.
paṭisandhāya.example_2: Jātā amittā duve sahāyā, paṭisandhāya caranti kissa hetu.
paṭisandhāya.translation_2: how is it that these two, who have become enemies, now go about with mutual connection?

vitihāraṃ.meaning_2: exchange; mutual sharing; exchange of food
vitihāraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text accusative singular. Probably a compound of viti (mutual) + hāra (taking, carrying).
vitihāraṃ.translation_2: The Videhan King, having gone to the upper palace, saw the exchange of each other's food;

medisā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Doubtful and rare form, occurring only in the verse yassa medisā paṇḍitā kulamhi (Jātaka 104). Probably an indeclinable adverb meaning 'such, of such a kind', modifying paṇḍitā; possibly a sandhi or corrupt variant of medhāvā or similar. Not to be confused with medinī, 'the earth'.
medisā.example_2: 104. Lābhā vata me anapparūpā, yassa medisā paṇḍitā kulamhi;
medisā.translation_2: How fortunate indeed for me, in whose family there are such wise ones,

paṇaye.meaning_2: should administer; should carry out; should establish
paṇaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular (paṇaye < paṇayeyya; eyya becomes e). Passages are verse; sāmaṃ appaṭivekkhiya means 'without having examined it himself'.
paṇaye.translation_2: An aristocrat should administer punishment without having examined it himself.

daṇḍiyañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text daṇḍiyaṃ is masculine accusative singular, combined with ca in the sandhi daṇḍiyañca. It contrasts with adaṇḍiya.
daṇḍiyañca.example_2: 108. Adaṇḍiyaṃ daṇḍayati [daṇḍiyati (syā. pī.)], daṇḍiyañca adaṇḍiyaṃ [adaṇḍiya (niyya), na daṇḍaye (?)];
daṇḍiyañca.translation_2: He punishes one who should not be punished, and one who should be punished, he does not punish;

vohātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Irregular imperfect 3rd singular of voharati; variant reading to voharituṃ in the edition. In the sense of 'to speak, declare'.
vohātu.translation_1: And instructs after having seen clearly, he indeed deserves to speak.

veravā.meaning_2: hostile; harbouring enmity; full of hatred
veravā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Predicative nominative singular in the verse; means one who has enmity (vera). Sometimes analysed as veravā = vera + vant, with -vā the contracted form of -vant.
veravā.example_2: 111. Paribhūto mudu hoti, atitikkho ca veravā;
veravā.translation_2: One who is malleable is despised, and one who is too severe is hated;

labheyyito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form labheyyito is labheyya + iti (quotation). The optative expresses a wish: 'may he also attain this'. The critical apparatus suggests ahāsopi / pahāsopi.
labheyyito.example_2: Tato naṃ nānukampati, aho sopi [ahāsopi (ka. sī. syā. ka.)] labheyyito.
labheyyito.translation_2: Then he does not sympathise with him, thinking, 'Alas, may he also attain this.'

kelāyito.meaning_2: cherished; fondled; treated affectionately; made much of
kelāyito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Preceded by hoti in the text, so nominative singular agreeing with the subject. The commentary glosses it as affectionate fondling; it could also be read as a passive causative participle of √kel.
kelāyito.translation_2: Then he becomes affectionate, and welcomes him with his speech.

guyhittho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the verse. In the text it agrees with manto and qualifies a mantra that 'conceals' its meaning; the printed form -ittho is unusual, perhaps a sandhi or metrical variant of guyho.
guyhittho.example_2: Mā cassu me pucchito nāmagottaṃ, guyhittho atthaṃ [mā taṃ (sī. syā. pī.)] vijaheyya manto [vijaheyyumantā (syā.)].
guyhittho.translation_2: ‘Do not, when questioned, conceal my name and lineage, lest the hymn abandon you.’

iso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative reading iso for īso in the text; nominative singular. Some editions read īsa (antelope?) here.
iso.example_1: 15. Isso [iso (sī.), īso (syā. pī.)] vanāni carasi, samāni visamāni ca;
iso.translation_1: “You range the woods, both even and uneven, as a king;

upakhandhamhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in the text (upakhandhamhā). Usually spelled upakkhandha; the meaning is the front or upper part of the shoulder.
upakhandhamhā.example_1: 21. Issassa [imassa (ka. sī. ka.)] upakkhandhamhā [upakhandhamhā (ka. sī. pī. ka.)], ukkacca caturaṅgulaṃ;
upakhandhamhā.translation_1: “From shoulder of the king of beasts cut off four inches wide,

māvivadittha.meaning_2: do not dispute; do not quarrel
māvivadittha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā (prohibitive particle) and vivadittha, the aorist 2nd plural of vivadati (dispute). The v.l. mā vivadatha has the present. One form of the verse line.
māvivadittha.example_1: Sammodatha mā vivadatha [māvivadittha (sī. syā. pī.)], mā hotha issaphandanā.
māvivadittha.translation_1: Be of one mind, and quarrel not, as beast and tree have done.

vigeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for viyeti / vineti in the verse; glossed by the commentary as vigacchati. Third person singular present in the text.
vigeti.example_1: 28. Savanena ekassa piyā bhavanti, disvā panekassa viyeti [vineti (syā.), viheti (pī.), vigeti (ka. aṭṭha.)] chando;
vigeti.translation_1: “By hearing, some become pleasant, and by seeing, desire fades away;

pariṇetvā.meaning_2: having taken around; having led around; having been led in marriage
pariṇetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of pariggahetvā in this verse; glossed as 'having taken around, having drawn near'. If derived from pariṇayati, v.l. for parinetvā.
pariṇetvā.translation_1: As he rolled the wheel of empire, obeisance done, he said this:

mupayanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text shows mupayanti; the initial m is assimilated from the preceding neva (na + eva) or is a sandhi variant. Read as upayanti, 3rd plural present of upayāti (√yā with prefix upa).
mupayanti.example_2: Ettāvatā padesaṃ te, nāgā neva mupayanti.
mupayanti.translation_2: Hither drive them, they will surely come thus far, but come no nigher.”

sampesito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally of the nāga in the verse. Nominative singular in the text. Some editions read sampesito as a contracted sandhi of saṃ + pesito.
sampesito.example_2: 75. Sampesito ca raññā, nāgo koñcova abhinaditvāna;
sampesito.translation_2: “Pierced, the creature trumpets loudly, shrill as any heron cries,

abhinaditvāna.meaning_2: having sounded forth; having trumpeted; having cried out
abhinaditvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of abhinadati (abhi + √nad); used of an elephant trumpeting. The form is not in the given related entries, so the analysis is inferred.
abhinaditvāna.example_2: 75. Sampesito ca raññā, nāgo koñcova abhinaditvāna;
abhinaditvāna.translation_2: “Pierced, the creature trumpets loudly, shrill as any heron cries,

paṭiosakkitvā.meaning_2: having drawn back; having retreated; having shrunk back
paṭiosakkitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of paṭisakkitvā; the cpd is paṭi + osakkitvā, from √sakk (move). Absolutive in -tvā.
paṭiosakkitvā.translation_1: Moved, then fell upon his haunches neath the weight, and could not rise.”

sannipātayi.meaning_2: causes to assemble; brings together; collects
sannipātayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative. The text form sannipātayi is a shortened aorist (or eastern aorist) 3rd singular used in verse; the present stem is sannipātaya-. PEU lists it as kā,kri 'he caused to gather'. Could also be read as aorist of sannipātayati.

akattiṃ.meaning_2: name of a sage (Akitti); one who performs no action
akattiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of Akitti, a sage, in Jātaka verse 83; accusative singular in the text. The PEU entry points to a different word, akattu.
akattiṃ.example_1: 83. Akittiṃ [akattiṃ (ka.)] disvā sammantaṃ, sakko bhūtapatī bravi;
akattiṃ.translation_1: On seeing Akitti living the holy life, Sakka, the lord of beings, said:

mavhayāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of āmavhayamāna; the snake is called mavhaya (Skt. mandūka). Nominative singular of a present participle in the sentence, modifying bheko. See √vhe (call, name).
mavhayāno.example_1: 104. Ahameva dubbhāsitaṃ bhāsi bālo, bhekovaraññe ahimavhāyamāno [mavhayāno (sī. pī.)];
mavhayāno.translation_1: I myself, the fool, spoke an ill-spoken word, like a frog in the forest calling to a snake;

tuṇḍilamanupucchiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] tuṇḍilaṃ (accusative singular of the proper name Tuṇḍila) + anupucchiṃ (aorist 1st singular of anupucchati).
tuṇḍilamanupucchiṃ.example_2: 106. Kimevahaṃ tuṇḍilamanupucchiṃ, kareyya saṃ [kareyyāsaṃ (syā.), kareyya sa (ka.), bhareyya saṃ (?)] bhātaraṃ kāḷikāyaṃ [kāḷikāya (syā. ka.)];
tuṇḍilamanupucchiṃ.translation_2: Why did I ask about Tundila, who would put forth the brother of Kālī;

accupatī.meaning_2: sparrow?; small bird?; bird flying across; bird that jumps between
accupatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare compound in Jātaka verse (Ja 107), describing the fork-tailed bird (kuliṅga) that flies across between two fighting rams. Uncertain analysis; perhaps acca (very) + upatī, or a form of upati.
accupatī.example_2: 107. Yo yujjhamānānamayujjhamāno [yujjhamānena ayujjhamāno (ka.)], meṇḍantaraṃ accupatī kuliṅgo;
accupatī.translation_2: The fork-tail that flies between two fighting rams without being part of the fight;

kuliṅgo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the verse. A small bird that flies between two fighting rams; the PEU derivation ku + √liṅg + a is uncertain.
kuliṅgo.example_2: 107. Yo yujjhamānānamayujjhamāno [yujjhamānena ayujjhamāno (ka.)], meṇḍantaraṃ accupatī kuliṅgo;
kuliṅgo.translation_2: The fork-tail that flies between two fighting rams without being part of the fight;

avakkhipantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine nominative singular avakkhipantī in the text. The woman is compared to a goat kicking against a bamboo clump, hitting the knife.
avakkhipantī.example_2: 109. Ajā yathā veḷugumbasmiṃ baddhā [bandhaṃ (syā. ka.)], avakkhipantī asimajjhagacchi;
avakkhipantī.translation_2: As a she-goat bound in a bamboo clump, kicking, met a knife;

galayā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In sandhi: galayā = gala + ī? No — galayā is instrumental singular of gala, with -āya → -yā; the text likely reads galakāvakantaṃ (galakaṃ + avakantaṃ), 'throat cut'. The variant galayā vikantuṃ is a commentary gloss. The form is instrumental.
galayā.example_1: Teneva tassā galakāvakantaṃ [galayā vikantuṃ (ka.), galakaṃ vikantā (syā.)], ayampi attho bahutādisova.
galayā.translation_1: By that same thing her throat was cut; this meaning is just like that.

paricitto.meaning_2: whose mind is grasped by others; known by others' minds; (commentarial: affected by others' thoughts)
paricitto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse sabbo loko paricitto aticitto, paricitto is nominative singular masculine of paricitta, agreeing with loko. The variant paracittena aticitto suggests the sense 'full of other minds'; paricitto is possibly a sandhi or variant of paracitta. Compare cittavā in the next line. The commentary may explain differently.
paricitto.example_2: 115. Sabbo loko paricitto aticitto [paracittena aticitto (sī. syā.), paracittena acitto (sī. aṭṭha.)], sabbo loko cittavā samhi citte;
paricitto.translation_2: The whole world is full of different minds, the whole world has a mind in the mind;

cittavā.meaning_2: having a mind; possessing thought; endowed with mind
cittavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse sabbo loko cittavā samhi citte, cittavā is the masculine nominative singular of cittavant used with loko. The related PEU entry cittavasī is not the same word: cittavā is a direct possessive adjective from citta + vant, not cittavasa + ī; and cittavā is nominative singular, not a separate lemma.
cittavā.example_2: 115. Sabbo loko paricitto aticitto [paracittena aticitto (sī. syā.), paracittena acitto (sī. aṭṭha.)], sabbo loko cittavā samhi citte;
cittavā.translation_2: The whole world is full of different minds, the whole world has a mind in the mind;

māhaṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Irregular aorist, 3rd plural of brūti (also brūhenti); metrically māhaṃsu for abruviṃsu / bruvanti. Not a negated (mā + ahaṃsu) form, though it could be misread that way in verse; the sense in these jātaka lines is 'they say / they said'.
māhaṃsu.example_2: 123. Saccaṃ kireva māhaṃsu, narā ekacciyā idha;
māhaṃsu.translation_2: People here speak truly, it is said;

tvevekacci.meaning_2: but (na tu); even (eva); some; a certain
tvevekacci.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution: na tu eva ekacci (na + tu > na tveva). ekacci means 'some, a certain' (indefinite); literally 'not indeed [is] a certain man [better?]'.
tvevekacci.example_1: Kaṭṭhaṃ niplavitaṃ seyyo, na tvevekacci yo naro.
tvevekacci.translation_1: It is better to rescue a log than a certain kind of person.

yamuddhariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of uddharati, with the sandhi form yamuddhariṃ = yaṃ + uddhariṃ. The text is verse, so the form is used for rhythm.

etadakkhā.meaning_2: this saw; saw this; told this
etadakkhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of etaṃ (pron) + akkhā (aorist of akkhāti, 'told'). The text has etadakkhā; the commentary glosses as 'told this'. Third person singular aorist.
etadakkhā.example_2: na cāpi me koci naṃ etadakkhā;

tuṇṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nunno in the verse; past participle of √tur 'hurry', used here in the sense 'released (quickly)'. The PEU treats it as an indeclinable 'quickly', but the syntax of the sentence points to a participle agreeing with saro.
tuṇṇo.example_1: Nunno [nuṇṇo (ka. sī. syā.), tuṇṇo (ka.)] saro sarabhaṃ hantu khippaṃ, annañhi etaṃ varapañña rañño.
tuṇṇo.translation_1: Let the released arrow quickly strike the Sarabha deer, for this, O wise one, is food for a king.

paricāriyanto.meaning_2: being attended (by); being served (by); being waited on (by)
paricāriyanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Masculine nominative singular agreeing with the addressee (the king); the agent is in the instrumental (nārīgaṇehi). Causative passive sense.
paricāriyanto.example_2: Nārīgaṇehi paricāriyanto, modassu raṭṭhe tidiveva vāsavo.
paricāriyanto.translation_2: Attended by groups of women, rejoice in the kingdom like Vasava in the heaven of the Thirty-three.

ujjhuntu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative plural of a causative formation, printed as an alternative to oḍḍentu in the text.
ujjhuntu.example_1: 3. Oḍḍentu [ujjhuntu (syā. ka.) aṅguttaranikāye passitabbaṃ] vāḷapāsāni, yathā vajjhetha so dijo;
ujjhuntu.translation_1: “Set a horsehair snare, so that this bird may be captured;

iṇadānaṃ.meaning_2: debt payment; repayment of debt; lending money (at interest)
iṇadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of iṇa (debt) and dāna (giving, payment). Nominative and accusative singular in the verse; it heads a list of livelihoods together with kasivāṇijjā.

hātūna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tūna from harati (√har 1), with the root vowel lengthened. In the text it describes carrying food to the young with the beak. The PEU entry hātuna is the same form.
hātūna.example_2: Tesaṃ tuṇḍena hātūna, muñce pubbakataṃ [pubbe kataṃ (sī.)] iṇaṃ.
hātūna.translation_2: Having carried [food] to them with my beak, I release the debt performed previously.”

tavassabyamhi.meaning_2: in the hermitage; in the ascetic's dwelling
tavassabyamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading tavassabyamhi (see ka.) has the same meaning. Locative singular in the text; cp. tavassamaṅgaṇa.
tavassabyamhi.example_1: 15. Bhuttañca pītañca tavassamamhi [tavassabyamhi (ka.)], rattiñca [ratī ca (sī. pī.)] no kosiya te sakāse;
tavassabyamhi.translation_1: “Having eaten and drunk in your hermitage, and [enjoyed] the night, Kosiya, in your presence;

santappayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist or causative form in -i used as a past tense in the verse; dpd peū splits saṃ + tapa + ṇaya + ī. Alternatively an aorist of santappati. Takes an object in the accusative (samaṇabrāhmaṇe).
santappayi.example_2: Annena pānena pasannacitto, santappayi samaṇabrāhmaṇe cāti.
santappayi.translation_2: With a pleased mind, through food and drink, he satisfied ascetics and brahmins, and so on.”

osaṭṭhi.meaning_2: sinking (into); affliction; alternative reading for osīdi
osaṭṭhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for osīdi in the verse, with osadhi (sī. syā. pī.) and osati (abhinavaṭīkā) as other readings; the meaning is uncertain, so this may be a misreading rather than a distinct word.
osaṭṭhi.example_1: 19. Osīdi [osadhi (sī. syā. pī.), osaṭṭhi (ka.), osati (abhinavaṭīkā), osīdati (?)] me dukkhaṃ [dukkhaṃ me (sī. pī.)] hadayaṃ, me ḍayhate nitammāmi;
osaṭṭhi.translation_1: My suffering has sunk into my heart, it is burning, I am exhausted;

osati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of osīdati in the Jātaka verse; ava- > o-. Only the 3rd singular occurs here.
osati.example_1: 19. Osīdi [osadhi (sī. syā. pī.), osaṭṭhi (ka.), osati (abhinavaṭīkā), osīdati (?)] me dukkhaṃ [dukkhaṃ me (sī. pī.)] hadayaṃ, me ḍayhate nitammāmi;
osati.translation_1: My suffering has sunk into my heart, it is burning, I am exhausted;

milayāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of milāyāmi (1st person singular present) in the verse; some editions read miyyāmi. 1sg present in the text.
milayāmi.example_1: 20. Tiṇamiva vanamiva milāyāmi [milayāmi (sī.), miyyāmi (sī. pī. aṭṭha.)], nadī aparipuṇṇāva [aparipuṇṇiyāva (sī. pī.)] sussāmi;
milayāmi.translation_1: I wither like grass, like a tree; I dry up like a river that is not full;

ayyire.meaning_2: venerable sir; reverend sir; noble one
ayyire.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metathesis of ariya (y and r swapped). Used in address (vocative) in the verse. The manuscript variant ayyire is likely a sandhi or spelling for ayyira before brahme.
ayyire.example_1: 42. Vande te ayirabrahme [ayyire brahme (ka.)], yo me icchitaṃ patiṃ varākiyā;
ayyire.translation_1: I revere you, noble brahmin, who gave me back my beloved husband, a wretched woman's [husband];

makā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. pī.) for akāsi in these verses; 3rd singular aorist of karoti. In pada 1 the subject is vihaṅgamo, in pada 2 mā ... makāsi is prohibitive.
makā.translation_1: It is too difficult to do, the work the bird did for the egg-born;
makā.example_2: Mā me paripanthamakāsi [makā (sī. pī.)], saggaṃ mama patthayānassa ’’.
makā.translation_2: Do not cause an obstacle for me, aspiring for heaven.”

yañcaretha.meaning_2: that a son should practise (for his father); which a son should perform
yañcaretha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text yaṃ ... caretha is written yañcaretha. The variant pitu yañcaretha shows the same sandhi. Caretha is optative 2nd plural of carati; the subject putto is construed with the singular sense. Alternative resolution yaṃ + caretha. In yaṃ care the same phrase resolves as yaṃ + care.
yañcaretha.example_1: 53. Addhā hi tāta satamesa dhammo, putto pitu yaṃ care [pitunaṃ care (ka.), pitu yañcaretha (sī. pī.)] atthacariyaṃ;
yañcaretha.translation_1: Yes, dear, this is the Dhamma of the wise, that a son should perform the duty of a father;

suhaddayañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of su + hadayaṃ. The variant suhaddayaṃ in the text. In the verse, part of the phrase 'make friends and companions'.
suhaddayañca.example_1: 56. Mittañca kayirātha suhadayañca [suhaddayañca (sī.), sakhāgharañca (pī.)], ayirañca kayirātha sukhāgamāya;
suhaddayañca.translation_1: One should make friends and companions, and one should make a noble one for the sake of happiness;

kojova.meaning_2: like a blanket; like a carpet
kojova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nivatthakocova in the same verse; the text prints kojova, with kojo (nom. sg. of kojava) + va (iva).
kojova.example_1: Nivatthakocova [kojova (sī. pī.)] sarebhihantvā, modāma puttehi samaṅgibhūtā.
kojova.translation_1: Like one who has put on clothes, after having conquered, we rejoice, united with our children.

evaṃkaro.meaning_2: one who acts thus; doing like this; acting in this way
evaṃkaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text evaṃkaro is nominative singular masculine, used substantively of a person (brāhmaṇo, samaṇo, macco).
evaṃkaro.example_1: Evaṃkaro brāhmaṇo hoti khemī, dhamme ṭhitaṃ tena amāpayiṃsu.
evaṃkaro.translation_1: One who does this is a brahmin and is peaceful; they said he is firm in Dhamma.
evaṃkaro.example_2: Samaṇo caraṃ hitvā mamāyitāni, evaṃkaro saggamupeti ṭhānaṃ.
evaṃkaro.translation_2: A samaṇa, conducting himself having abandoned attachments, one who acts thus achieves the heavenly mansion.

gharamāvasātu.meaning_2: dwells at home; remains in the house
gharamāvasātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of gharaṃ + āvasati. In the text the phrase apassaṃ gharamāvasātu is an optative or imperative wish: 'may he dwell at home not seeing (his own aging)'. The form appears to be āvasātu (3rd sg. imperative/optative of āvasati), though written without the initial ā after gharaṃ.
gharamāvasātu.example_2: Vayaṃ apassaṃ gharamāvasātu, bhisāni te brāhmaṇa yo ahāsi.
gharamāvasātu.translation_2: May he dwell at home not seeing his own aging, he who stole your lotus-roots, Brahmin.

mahimāvasātu.meaning_2: may he rule the earth; may he inhabit the earth
mahimāvasātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mahimaṃ (locative of mahī, 'earth') and avasātu, 3rd singular imperative of avasati in the sense of ruling or inhabiting; the sandhi is unusual and the reading may be corrupt. Alternatively the first element could be mahiṃ with -a- before vasātu.
mahimāvasātu.example_2: Sa cāturantaṃ mahimāvasātu, bhisāni te brāhmaṇa yo ahāsi.
mahimāvasātu.translation_2: May he rule the earth to its four ends, he who stole your lotus-roots, Brahmin.

carātu.meaning_2: let him walk; let him go; let him practice
carātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular of carati, used three times in the verse with the sense 'let it go' or 'let him roam'. The form is carātu, with the imperative ending -tu.

bajjhatū.meaning_2: is bound; is tied; is attached (to); is caught (by)
bajjhatū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular (bajjhatū) in the text, expressing a wish. √bandh with the ya sign gives bajjha-.
bajjhatū.example_2: 89. So bajjhatū pāsasatehi chabbhi [chamhi (sī. pī.), chassu (?)], rammā vanā niyyatu rājadhāniṃ [rājaṭhāniṃ (ka.)];
bajjhatū.translation_2: May he be bound by six-fold ropes and led from the pleasant forest to the capital city;

rājaṭhāniṃ.meaning_2: capital city; royal seat; king's residence
rājaṭhāniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of rājadhānī (see Sinhalese edition; also printed rājadhāniṃ). Accusative singular in the verse, after niyyatu. Compound of rāja + ṭhānī, from √ṭhā, but treated as a compound, so root fields are empty.
rājaṭhāniṃ.example_1: 89. So bajjhatū pāsasatehi chabbhi [chamhi (sī. pī.), chassu (?)], rammā vanā niyyatu rājadhāniṃ [rājaṭhāniṃ (ka.)];
rājaṭhāniṃ.translation_1: May he be bound by six-fold ropes and led from the pleasant forest to the capital city;

vupatthambha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vi + upatthambha (vi + u > vu). Locative singular in the verse, meaning 'on what ground / with what support'. Sometimes analysed as a contraction of upatthambha.
vupatthambha.example_2: Kismiṃ vupatthambha sahassanetta, isīhi tvaṃ kīḷasi devarāja.
vupatthambha.translation_2: On what grounds, O Thousand-Eyed one, do you play with ascetics, O King of Gods?

dhammacāriṇī.meaning_2: acting in accordance with the Dhamma; practising the Dhamma; righteous
dhammacāriṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form dhammacāriṇī in the text, nominative singular. The separation is dhamma + cārī (from √car 1).
dhammacāriṇī.translation_1: I, finding delight in non-violence, am a follower of the Dhamma;

samacāriṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of samacārin; nominative singular modifying a woman, used of a faithful wife in the verse. Sometimes spelled samacārinī.
samacāriṇī.example_1: 122. Itthiyo [itthiyā (pī.)] jīvalokasmiṃ, yā hoti [honti (sī. syā.)] samacārinī [samacāriṇī (sī.)];
samacāriṇī.translation_1: In the world of living beings, a woman who is a faithful wife,

kapotiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form kapotiyā in the text is either instrumental singular ('by/with the female pigeon') or dative/genitive singular ('for/of the female pigeon'), depending on interpretation; the commentary-style gloss takes it as 'consumed by desire for'.
kapotiyā.example_2: 128. Ahaṃ pure giddhigato kapotiyā, asmiṃ padesasmimubho ramāma;
kapotiyā.translation_2: “I was formerly consumed by desire for a female pigeon; in this place we both delighted.

kapotiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine of kapota. Accusative singular in the text (kapotiṃ).
kapotiṃ.example_2: Athaggahī sākuṇiko kapotiṃ, akāmako tāya vinā ahosiṃ.
kapotiṃ.translation_2: Then a fowler caught the female pigeon; against my will, I was without her.”

kanditva.meaning_2: having cried; having wailed; having lamented
kanditva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā, written kanditva (shortened final vowel) in the verse. Used with roditvā in the sentence.
kanditva.example_1: 132. Tato janā nikkhamitvāna gāmā, kanditvā roditvā [kanditva roditva (sī.)] apakkamiṃsu;
kanditva.translation_1: “Then the people, having come out from the village, having lamented and wept, departed.

sosayuṃ.meaning_2: causes to dry up; makes dry; dries up
sosayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of sussati. In the text the aorist 3rd plural sosayuṃ is used: 'they dried up'.
sosayuṃ.example_2: Uṇho ca vāto tikhiṇā ca rasmiyo, te sosayuṃ tassa karīsamaggaṃ.
sosayuṃ.translation_2: The hot wind and the sharp rays [of the sun] dried up the passage for excrement.

temayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative temeti. The PEU entry temayī = [timu+ṇaya+ī] supports the analysis as a causative aorist; so temayī tassa karīsamaggaṃ = "it moistened his excrement path".
temayī.example_2: Mahā ca megho sahasā pavassi, so temayī tassa karīsamaggaṃ.
temayī.translation_2: A vast cloud rained down suddenly; it moistened that passage for excrement.

nikkhamisaṃ.meaning_2: will go out (from); will leave; will depart (from)
nikkhamisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular future in -issaṃ of the nikkhamati series, meaning 'I will go out (from)'. Cando yathā rāhumukhā pamutto is a simile for being released.
nikkhamisaṃ.example_2: 136. Tato ahaṃ nikkhamisaṃ bhadante, cando yathā rāhumukhā pamutto;
nikkhamisaṃ.translation_2: Then I exited, Venerable Sir, like the moon released from the jaws of Rahu.

kipillikāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the plural kipillikāni (ni-nighaṇḍu); nominative/accusative plural of an a-stem.
kipillikāni.example_2: 137. Vammīkathūpasmiṃ kipillikāni, nippothayanto tuvaṃ pure carāsi;
kipillikāni.translation_2: “You used to roam around destroying the ants on the ant-hill.

paripothayiṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural (paripothayiṃsu) in both verses, with patient maṃ; causative of pari + √puṭh, 'struck on all sides'.
paripothayiṃsu.example_2: Tato janā nikkhamitvāna gāmā, kodaṇḍakena paripothayiṃsu maṃ.
paripothayiṃsu.translation_2: Then the people, having come out from the village, beat me with bows.

bandhitva.meaning_2: having tied; having bound; having caught; having formed
bandhitva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written bandhitva in the text, a variant of bandhitvā; sandhi with the following morādhipatiṃ in the verse.
bandhitva.example_1: Bandhitvā [bandhitva (sī. pī.)] morādhipatiṃ yasassiṃ, dukkhā sa pamucci [dukkhā pamucci (sī.), dukkhā pamuñci (syā. pī.)] yathāhaṃ pamuttoti.
bandhitva.translation_1: The glorious lord of peacocks he set free From pain, as soon as he was caught, like me.

nitāḷeti.meaning_2: strikes down; beats down; knocks down
nitāḷeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the first sentence 'tañca seno nitāḷeti' the hawk is the agent ('the hawk strikes that one'). PEU analysis ni + taḷa + ṇe + ti agrees, though the vowel is lengthened before the causative suffix.
nitāḷeti.example_2: Tañca seno nitāḷeti, veyyagghiyeva sā gati.
nitāḷeti.translation_2: The hawk strikes that one; such is the way of the tiger.

appodavaṇṇe.meaning_2: of the appearance of waterless rice-gruel; pale like waterless milk-rice; (of food) of plain colour, unappetising-looking
appodavaṇṇe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound of appa (little, without) + uda (water) + vaṇṇa (colour, appearance); the PEU splits it as appoda + vaṇṇa. In the verse it agrees with kummāse (masculine accusative plural), describing thick rice-gruel of plain appearance.
appodavaṇṇe.example_2: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
appodavaṇṇe.translation_2: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

siṅgīnti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the verse. The commentary glosses siṅgiṃ with siṅgivera, ginger. The -ti is the quotation particle.
siṅgīnti.example_1: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
siṅgīnti.translation_1: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

vidalaṃ.meaning_2: split pulse; chopped beans (esp. mung beans); pieces of split bean
vidalaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it occurs in the compound vidalasūpiyo (accusative singular before sūpiyo?). The commentary glosses vidalasūpādayo as muggasūpādayo, i.e. bean soup and the like.
vidalaṃ.example_1: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
vidalaṃ.translation_1: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

paṭiyāni.meaning_2: response; counter-present; return gift; something given in return
paṭiyāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a list of valuable items in a Jātaka verse; probably a gift given in return or a matching present. Doubtful: could be read as paṭi + yāna (a return journey) or as a variant of paṭiyāṇa (a belt or ornament).
paṭiyāni.translation_2: Silver in handfuls, precious rugs, and jewels manifold;

uddiyāni.meaning_2: fringed (blankets); with fringes at both ends
uddiyāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adjective agreeing with kambalā (neuter plural) in the verse; not a headword by itself. The dictionary form is uddiya (PEU: uddiya, from ubhaya + dasā, 'fringed at both ends'). Spelling variant uddiyāne in some editions.
uddiyāni.example_2: 192. Kāsikāni ca vatthāni, uddiyāni ca kambalā [uddiyāne ca kambale (sī. pī.)];
uddiyāni.translation_2: And robes of fine Benares cloth, and blankets thick and thin.

uddiyāne.meaning_2: blanket with fringes on both ends; double-fringed woollen blanket
uddiyāne.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads uddiyāni (nominative plural) beside kambalā; some editions have uddiyāne. PEU suggests a derivation ubhaya + dasā, but the form is doubtful. Likely a kind of blanket.
uddiyāne.example_1: 192. Kāsikāni ca vatthāni, uddiyāni ca kambalā [uddiyāne ca kambale (sī. pī.)];
uddiyāne.translation_1: And robes of fine Benares cloth, and blankets thick and thin.

nāridā.meaning_2: giving women; bestowing maidens (said of a tree branch)
nāridā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A poetic compound describing the western branch as giving/bestowing beautiful women (nāri + √dā). Occurs only in this verse; the related entry analyses it as nāri + dā + a, a ti-stem adjective. Nominative singular in the text.
nāridā.example_2: Nāridā pacchimā sākhā, sabbakāme ca uttarā;
nāridā.translation_2: The western gave us pretty maids, the northern all things good:

mādīnavaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In mādīnavaṃ the sandhi is eta + idaṃ > etaṃ, but metrically the vowel is lengthened as etā, then elided to mā before ādīnavaṃ. The word is the genitive plural of eta, "of these (evils)"; the lines read etaṃ ādīnavaṃ, "this danger". The first pāda scans evaṃ (so the variant eta matches). Alternative analysis: mā + ādīnavaṃ, "the danger of Māra".
mādīnavaṃ.example_1: 201. Eva [eta (sī. pī.)] mādīnavaṃ ñatvā, taṇhā dukkhassa sambhavaṃ;
mādīnavaṃ.translation_1: So let him, seeing this evil thing, pain rooted in desire,

sādhīno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of the king of Mithilā; variant reading sādhino in the text. The PEU splits it as sa + adhīna, but as a name the compound analysis is doubtful.
sādhīno.example_1: 205. Tato ca rājā sādhino [sādhīno (sī. pī.)], vedeho mithilaggaho [pamukho rathamāruhi (sī. pī.)];
sādhīno.translation_1: 205. Then King Sādhina, the ruler of Mithilā, of Videha, mounted the vehicle;

cāhametamicchāmi.grammar: sandhi, ind + pron + pron + pron + pr
cāhametamicchāmi.meaning_2: and I do not desire this
cāhametamicchāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca + ahaṃ + etaṃ + na + icchāmi (na + icchāmi contracted to micchāmi with sandhi). Found in Jātaka verse 213.
cāhametamicchāmi.translation_2: 213. 'I do not desire this which comes from a gift from another;

vaname.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form vaname is probably vanaṃ + e or a mis-segmentation of vanamige; if it is really vana + e it is a separate sandhi form. The PEU entries point to vana + miga.

viciya.meaning_2: having investigated; having examined; having analysed; having discerned
viciya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for vicayaṃ in the verse; the same form would be absolutive of vicināti. The commentary reading is vicayaṃ, a noun in apposition.
viciya.example_1: Tesaṃ vibhaṅgaṃ vicayaṃ [viciya (ka.)], vitthārena suṇohi me.
viciya.translation_1: Listen to me as I explain their classification in detail.

ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of three fruit names (amba, jambu, vibhītaka) in the verse; the Burmese and Sinhalese editions read them separately. Accusative singular in the text.
ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.example_1: 242. Harītakaṃ [harīṭakaṃ (bahūsu)] āmalakaṃ, ambaṃ jambuṃ vibhītakaṃ [ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ (sī. pī.)];
ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.translation_1: Myrobalan, gooseberry, mango, rose-apple, belleric myrobalan,

aṇḍacchedā.meaning_2: castrator; one who cuts off the testicles
aṇḍacchedā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text a nominative plural in -ā, agreeing with nilañchakā. The related form aṇḍacchedaka is an adjective.
aṇḍacchedā.example_2: Bahū te [ne (syā. ka.)] paripucchanti, aṇḍacchedā nilañchakā [tilañchakā (pī.)].
aṇḍacchedā.translation_2: They question many people, they are gelded and marked.

āgodhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka verse paired with macchakacchapaṃ; possibly a lizard (iguana). The vowel of the final member appears shortened from godhā in the compound.
āgodhā.translation_2: They bind hares and cats, and hunt lizards, fish, and tortoises.

mupocitaṃ.meaning_2: and honoured; and served; and waited upon
mupocitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably sandhi of mu (variant of pi/su, emphatic) + upocitaṃ, pp of upa + √ci in the sense 'honoured; served'. The alternative reading mupocitaṃ with gloss (bahūsu) suggests uncertainty; it may instead be muditaṃ ('pleased') or a compound reading 'by many honoured'. Instrumental/locative context in the verse.
mupocitaṃ.translation_1: Endowed with the best gabled cells, and waited upon with a magnificent seat.

āmantaṇīyo.meaning_2: to be invited; to be addressed; to be spoken to
āmantaṇīyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling āmantaṇīyo in the text (āmantanīyo in other editions). Nominative singular of the potential participle, agreeing with the subject.
āmantaṇīyo.example_1: Garu ca āmantanīyo [āmantaṇīyo (sī. pī.)] ca, dātumarahāmi bhojanaṃ.
āmantaṇīyo.translation_1: He is respected and to be invited, I ought to give the food to him.

biḷālitakkaḷāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form biḷālitakkaḷāni in the text. Probably a compound of biḷāli (?) and takkaḷa (radish).
biḷālitakkaḷāni.example_1: 280. Khaṇantālukalambāni [khaṇamālukalambāni (syā. ka.)], bilālitakkalāni ca [biḷālitakkaḷāni ca (sī. pī.)];
biḷālitakkaḷāni.translation_1: Digging up bulbs and radishes, and lotus stalks;

saṃhāriyaṃ.meaning_2: to be gathered together; to be collected; to be drawn together
saṃhāriyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle (gerundive) in -ya of saṃharati; variant reading, the text's saṅghāriyaṃ is a scribal variant. Accusative singular neuter agreeing with sāmākanīvāraṃ; the sense 'gathering (millet and wild rice)' fits the verse.
saṃhāriyaṃ.example_1: Dhunaṃ sāmākanīvāraṃ, saṅghāriyaṃ pasāriyaṃ [saṃhāriyaṃ pahāriyaṃ (syā.), saṃsāriyaṃ pasāriyaṃ (ka.)].
saṃhāriyaṃ.translation_1: Shaking out millet and wild rice, gathering and spreading them.

kharājinaso.meaning_2: with a black leopard's hide; covered with a dark antelope skin
kharājinaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a Jātaka verse list of names; probably a name or epithet (Kharājina). Vocative or nominative singular in the text; if read as khara + ajina + so, it is two words joined by sandhi.
kharājinaso.example_2: Suva kinnara mukka kharājinaso, bhisajāta mahesi kapotavaro;
kharājinaso.translation_2: Suva, Kinnara, Mukka, Kharājina, So, Bhisajāta, Mahesi, Kapotavaro;
